sections.description:
Fixed Amount of Central Excise Duty on Marriage Halls and Marriage Lawn
Rules 1994
Fixed
Amount of Central Excise Duty on Marriage Halls and Marriage Lawn Rules 1994
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part 11, 15th October, 1994]'
S.R.O. No.1016(I)/94, dated 11‑10‑1994.‑‑In
exercise of the powers conferred by subsection (9) of section 3 of the Central
Excises Act, 1944 (I of 1944), read with section 37 thereof, the Central Board
of Revenue, with the prior approval of the Federal Government, it pleased to
make the following rules for' the collection of fixed amount of central excise
duty from the operators of marriage halls or marriage lawns liable to pay the
duty in accordance with the Notification No. S.R.O. 1015 (1)\94, dated the 11th
October, 1994, namely:‑‑
1. Short title, application and commencement.‑‑(l) These rules may be called
the Fixed Amount of Central Excise Duty on Marriage Halls and Marriage Lawns
Rules, 1994..
(2) They
shall come into force at once.
(3) They shall apply to the operators of marriage halls and marriage
lawns who are liable to pay duty in accordance with the Notification No.S.R.O.
(1)\94, dated the 11th October, 1994.
2. Definitions.‑‑(l) In these Rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or
context,‑‑
(a)
"Act" means the Central Excises Act, 1944 (1 of 1944);
(b) "Assistant Collector" means the Assistant Collector of
Central Excise in whose jurisdiction the marriage hall or marriage lawn is
situated;
(c) "Association" means the respective association of operators
of marriage halls and marriage lawns;
(d) "Authorized officer" means an officer of central excise not
below the rank of Superintendent of Central Excise;
(e) "Joint Survey Committee' means Joint Survey Committee
constituted under sub‑rule (3) of rule 4:
(f) "marriage ceremony" means any ceremony related to wedding and
includes engagement, mehndi, nikah and valima receptions;
(g) "marriage hall or marriage lawn" means an enclosed or open
premises or place, whether or not covered with a "shamiana" or kanat,
or enclosed by walls grills, fences, hedges wherein marriage ceremonies are
held irrespective of any other use of such premises or place;
Explanation.‑For the purpose of these rules enclosed area shall
include halls, rooms, kitchens, toilets and any other area in use of the
operator of a marriage hall or marriage lawn;
(h) "Notification" means the Central Board of Revenue's
Notification No. S.R.O. 1015 (1)\94, dated the 11th October, 1994;
(i) "operator" means owner, lessee, manager or any other person
operating marriage hall or marriage lawn; and
(j) "Superintendent of Central Excise" means the Superintendent
of Central Excise in whose jurisdiction the marriage hall or the marriage lawn
is situated.
3. Operator of a marriage hall or marriage lawn to obtain licence.‑‑The operator shall, before
commencing the operation of a marriage hall or marriage lawn, obtain a licence
under rule 176 of Central Excise Rules, 1944.
4. Declaration to be made.‑‑(l) Every operator shall make a declaration in the prescribed pro forma
annexed to these Rules to the Assistant Collector within twenty days of the
commencement of these Rules, for the financial year 1994‑95.
(2) The declaration made under sub‑rule (1) shall also remain in
force during the financial year 1994‑95 unless the Notification is
rescinded earlier or the declaration is revoked by the operator as a result of
permanent closure of operation of marriage hall or, as the case may be,
marriage lawn:
Provided that the operator informs in writing to this effect the
Assistant Collector ten days before the aforesaid closure.
(3) The declaration made under sub‑rule (1) shall be verified by a
Joint Survey Committee comprising at least one nominee of the respective
Association, the Assistant Collector and the operator or his nominee.
